data.narrative:
Matter is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $21M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or valuation-tier density to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Only one valuation method is applicable given data constraints. The stage-progression method uses the $14M total-raised proxy as a base and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A advancement, implying a valuation of $35M. This reflects the anticipated increase in company value upon reaching the next funding round, conditional on execution and market conditions.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30M to $40M, with a median of $35M. However, this range rests on a single methodology. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently comparable peers at Matter's stage and valuation tier within robotics and manufacturing, which limits cross-sectional benchmarking. Additionally, the stage-progression method is backward-looking and assumes typical multipliers; actual outcomes depend on the company's progress on technical milestones, customer traction, and capital market conditions at Series A. A more robust triangulation would require either disclosure of additional comparable transactions or later-stage data as the company matures.
